Uses `StaticHtmlRenderer`, not `HtmlRenderer`: `HtmlRootComponent` cannot take new parameters, so every prop change would re-run `OnInitializedAsync` and discard state; `RenderRootComponentAsync` keeps one instance across updates (`OnInitialized` once, `OnParametersSet` per change). **BOTH hosts, trimmed publish included** — `net10.0` and `net10.0-browser`, one code path with no `#if`; only the renderer's source differs (the ASP.NET shared framework on the server, the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web` package in the browser). Trimming was the real constraint and is now handled rather than disclaimed: `ParameterView.SetParameterProperties` reaches `[Parameter]` properties by reflection inside `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components`, on the hosted type, so under `PublishTrimmed` (a WASM app's DEFAULT) the trimmer removes the setters and the island renders as an EMPTY `<rask-blazor>` — no analyser warning (the reflection is in another assembly), no exception, nothing in the console, and a green build. `BlazorComponent<TComponent>` annotates its type parameter `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicProperties)]`, which states the requirement where the concrete type is known. Gated by the WASM showcase's Blazor island page (published trimmed on every build) plus a browser E2E asserting the hosted component's OUTPUT rather than the element's presence — an empty island passes a presence check — and by `TrimmingContractTests` in the unit gate. It is opt-in on both frameworks: neither TFM group of the `Rask` meta-package references it. The hosted type must come from a REFERENCED project or package for its parameters to be read — a `.razor` in the same project is produced by the Razor source generator and one source generator never sees another's output, so it works but unverified (RASK066). Diagnostics RASK061 (must be partial), RASK064 (name collision), RASK066. **Compiling `.razor` INTO the chain was investigated and rejected on facts**: Razor's syntax layer is `internal` in every shipped version (`RazorSyntaxTree.Root` returns a type no third party can name), the .NET 10 SDK compiler exposes neither the intermediate document nor a way to register a pass that would receive one — its 23 `InternalsVisibleTo` friends (`rzc`, Blazor's generator, the VS and VS Code Razor extensions) reach those instead — and the last public extension API is `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Language` 6.0.36, a .NET 6-era package out of support since November 2024. `@bind` round-trips, write-back included: a value-carrying event goes through Rask's INPUT channel (the one that ships the element's value beside the handler id) rather than the DOM-event table. Not yet: `OnAfterRender`/`IJSRuntime`/`ElementReference`, fine-grained diffing inside the island (a prop change replaces its DOM, losing scroll and selection), templated `RenderFragment<T>` parameters, and circuit mode.
- [Islands](docs/islands.md): a `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte` or Lit file as an **ordinary Rask component** — the other half of the front-end story from the SPA lane, and the opposite trade. Derive a component from `ReactComponent`, `VueComponent`, `SvelteComponent` or `LitComponent`, drop the front-end file beside it (paired by filename, exactly like `Counter.js` beside `Counter.cs`), and place it anywhere the chain goes: a leaf inside a card, a subtree, or the whole of a `[Route]` page's `Render()`. There is deliberately NO separate page concept — "React owns this route" is the case where the component IS the page root, so replaceability is a property of the COMPONENT rather than of the route and composes at every level of the tree. **The base class IS the declaration**: it names the runtime in the one place that cannot disagree with what actually mounts, which is also what lets a Lit component pair with `./Name.ts` by convention — a Lit file is ordinary TypeScript and no extension distinguishes it, so before this every Lit component had to name its module twice. The cost is the single-inheritance slot (a component already extending `BsBlock` cannot also be a `ReactComponent`), and that is the deliberate trade: chrome in Rask comes from the CHAIN, not from inheritance, so the answer is `BsCard[ Chart.Series(pts) ]` rather than inheriting both. Override `Module` with a CONSTANT string to point somewhere convention cannot reach — the bundler reads it at build time, so anything computed is RASK059. `partial` is required (RASK056) because the name, the module and the props writer are generated into the same class; a hand-written `Render()` is CS0239, because the base class SEALS it (a rule the type system can state needs no analyzer). **C# owns the props**: ordinary properties, so the chain and RASK001 apply unmodified, serialized by generated `Utf8JsonWriter` code rather than reflection (which is what lets them survive trimming/AOT), over the SAME wire vocabulary the CQRS codecs use — `WireShape` and the TypeScript emitter moved to `Rask.Generators.Shared` so there is one answer to "what does this C# type look like on the wire" instead of two that drift. A prop named after an HTML tag (`Title`, `Label`, `Data`, `Form`) does NOT compile — CS0108 against the chain entry, fatal under -warnaserror — which is not specific to these but far likelier here, because those are natural prop names for a UI component. **Callbacks re-enter C# over the channel every DOM handler already uses**: `Action`/`Action<T>`/`Func<Task>`/`Func<T,Task>` travel as a handler reference rather than a value, and reach the app over the open WebSocket on the Server host or a direct `[JSExport]` call into this tab's runtime on WASM — never a channel of its own, so a callback inherits sequence stamping, the queue-while-reconnecting and the auth suppression window for free, and the `.tsx` is byte-identical on both hosts. A callback prop also ESCALATES its page to interactive under the auto render ladder, exactly as `data-rask-on-click` does; without that a page whose only interactivity is a callback would be served as a static document and the first click would reach nobody. An unwired callback OMITS its key (the front end sees `undefined`); a null DATA prop stays JSON `null`, because "never set" and "set to nothing" differ. **The live diff treats the subtree as opaque** — React reconciles those nodes on its own schedule, and two writers on one subtree does not throw, it corrupts on the next parent re-render. `Component.OpaqueSubtree` rides `RenderFrame` so the differ skips by `SubtreeLength`, AND is written as `data-rask-opaque` so the client morph refuses to descend: both are needed, because the diff and the full-HTML fallback are separate paths to the same DOM, and the morph is the one that bites. `LeanFrame` carries the flag too, or the retained clean-subtree cache would replay a cached component without its boundary. What crosses is props and only props: a change travels as ONE attribute op the client routes to the adapter's `update`, so an update is a reconcile and never a remount (the component keeps scroll, focus, an open dropdown, a half-typed field), and callbacks keep their IDENTITY across updates because React compares props by identity. **An island is a LEAF**: it takes props and nothing else, and children are deliberately not offered. Its subtree belongs to another renderer, so Rask-rendered content handed inside one would still be content Rask owns and updates in nodes it can no longer address — EditOp paths are positional `childNodes` indices, and every one of them is wrong the moment the adapter relocates the nodes. Compose the other way round: the island goes INSIDE the Rask markup, and anything it must display crosses as a prop, where a change is a reconcile and keeps working. React, Vue, Svelte and Lit all ship; Preact rides the React adapter unchanged (an app-wide `preact/compat` alias, so it is a choice ONE bundle makes for every island in it), and the client runtime imports NO framework at all — each built chunk default-exports its own adapter, three functions wide (`mount`/`update`/`unmount`), so further runtimes are additive. `dotnet build` writes one entry module per component (pairing it with its adapter, so the `.tsx` keeps no Rask import) and hands Vite a generated config that builds a chunk each plus the manifest the runtime resolves names through — read back from the rollup ACTUALLY emitted rather than predicted, so a re-hashed chunk cannot drift from the entry pointing at it. **Node runs only when the project has a package.json**: that single probe is the gate, so an app with none of these never learns this package has a build step. Vite is the ONLY bundler and that is deliberate — an esbuild path with no npm was designed and rejected: esbuild can do the whole job (--splitting for a hashed chunk per component plus a shared one, --metafile for what was ACTUALLY emitted, --jsx=automatic, ~1ms) but two bundlers means two failure modes and "why does it work in project A but not B" forever, and the no-npm audience was narrower than it looked since a real Lit component imports `lit` from npm. Rask ITSELF stays npm-free (#871 fetches esbuild and tsgo as verified binaries); needing React from npm is inherent to asking for a React component. Vite is what made Vue and Svelte cheap, since their SFC compilers ARE Vite plugins; the single-file compilers must be registered BEFORE the React plugin, whose JSX transform is general and would otherwise swallow a `.vue` as `Unexpected JSX expression` at line 1. A `.vue`/`.svelte` cannot be checked by tsgo (no plugin seam), so those go to `vue-tsc`/`svelte-check` from the project's own node_modules — a second and third toolchain accepted because the alternative is not a weaker check but NO check. **Both hosts are verified in a browser**, not merely designed to work: the same byte-identical .tsx mounts, takes its C# props and round-trips a typed callback on Server (WebSocket) and on WASM ([JSExport] into this tab's runtime), with server state and React's own local state advancing together — which is what shows the adapter RECONCILES rather than remounts. That run found four faults nothing else could: colliding handler ids putting the callback in a map the dispatcher never reads; HeadAssets being collected only in the serializer's COMPONENT branch, so an element-shaped component rendered an empty <head> and no runtime script; Vite dropping `export default` from application entries without preserveEntrySignatures; and an Action<T> falling to a DynamicInvoke with no arguments, throwing, and taking the page down. Callback arguments are scalars for now. Not yet: Angular (viable via standalone components + `createApplication()`, but its build needs the Angular compiler rather than plain Vite), Blazor `.razor` components (props stay C#, never JSON), islands owned by a shared LIBRARY (the manifest is resolved app-rooted at `/_rask/external/manifest.json`), and SSR for the bundler-backed runtimes.
- [Batteries dashboard](docs/dashboard.md): the opt-in `Rask.Dashboard` package — an operator dashboard at `/_rask` over every DB-backed pillar's own table, no exporter or second datastore. Runs on the `server` template AND in a client-plus-host solution (in the `.Server` project, mounted at `/_rask/{**path}` above the SPA fallback, rendered through the shipped `RaskDashboardShell` root since a bundle-serving host owns no component for `UseRaskServer<TApp>` to name). `/_rask` is the framework's own reserved prefix — `/_rask/a/{hash}.{ext}` scoped assets, `/_rask/auth/redeem`, `/_rask/upload/{id}`, `/_rask/download/{id}/{token}` — which are LITERAL routes and so outrank the dashboard's catch-all; a dashboard page named `a`/`auth`/`upload`/`download` would silently 404 (pinned by ReservedPrefixTests). An app referencing BOTH hosts must spell its registrations `AddRaskServer()`/`AddRaskWasmHost()` and `UseRaskServer<T>()`/`UseRaskWasmHost()`: both packages declare `AddRask(this IServiceCollection)` and C# reports NO ambiguity — the WASM host's has no optional parameters and so wins the "fewer defaulted arguments" tie-break silently, leaving an app that starts with no live runtime and dies on its first request. `builder.Services.AddRaskDashboard<AppDbContext>()` (scaffolded by `rask new` — the dashboard is on by default, `--no-ops` leaves it out) mounts a route chain under a `[Route("_rask")]` layout. Panels: Overview (a tile per queue + a banner the moment any dead letter exists), Queues (outbox/jobs/mail in one view split due/delayed/FAILED/processed, expand a row for its last error + stored payload), Cache (keys, sizes, expiry, expired-not-yet-swept), Logs (bounded in-memory tail of the ILogger pipeline — memory-only, gone on restart), System (SQLite pragmas read live via the open DbConnection, DB size, recurring-job schedule joined to RecurringJobState). A panel appears ONLY when its battery is BOTH registered (its options singleton resolves) AND mapped (Model.FindEntityType) — the second half catches AddRaskX() without modelBuilder.AddRaskX(), where the service resolves but every query throws. FAILED = `ProcessedAt IS NULL AND Attempts >= MaxAttempts`, the inverse of the processors' drain query (there is no status column). SECURITY IS FAIL-CLOSED: pages carry `[Authorize(Policy = RaskDashboardPolicies.Access)]` on the LAYOUT (RouteAuthorizationGuard walks the chain, so it covers every page + re-checks on in-app nav); the default policy is installed with PostConfigure<AuthorizationOptions> so call order is irrelevant and an app-defined policy always wins — undefined => open in Development (with a banner) and DENY-ALL everywhere else. ACTIONS `o.Actions` (default Safe): retry a dead letter / retry all / purge processed / evict a cache key; `RaskDashboardActions.All` adds delete-a-row and flush-the-cache. Each is ONE ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete with the guard in the WHERE clause (never a tracked entity), so the DB evaluates it at write time and the dashboard can't raise a concurrency exception; the retry guard is the inverse of the drain query, so a row in flight is invisible to it and retry is safe against a live queue with no coordination. Panels poll `RefreshInterval` (2s), compare before re-rendering (idle => no diff, no WS traffic), and the loop is BOUNDED by `MaxPollDuration` (5min, then a Resume button) because every open tab competes for SQLite's single write lock. Backup tiles are opt-in via `IDashboardBackupProbe` — referencing Rask.SQLite.Snapshots/Litestream would drag a native SQLitePCLRaw provider bundle into every consumer and tie a provider-agnostic EF dashboard to SQLite.
- [Background jobs](docs/jobs.md): the opt-in `Rask.Jobs` package — durable background work on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). A job is an `IBackgroundJob` (: Rask.Cqrs ICommand), enqueued through `IJob`, run off the request thread by an ordinary `ICommandHandler<TJob>`. Inject `IJob` and `EnqueueAsync(job)` (run asap) / `ScheduleAsync(job, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `Job` row (Type name + JSON payload + RunAt) via IDbContextFactory (its OWN transaction — not atomic with a business change; use Rask.Outbox for that). The hosted `JobProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due jobs (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), dispatches each via IDispatcher.SendAsync((ICommand)job) in a fresh scope, stamps ProcessedAt; on failure Attempts++/Error and pushes RunAt out by exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped at MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 25) → then a dead letter kept for inspection; completed jobs purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d, Zero=keep). Durable interval-recurring: `o.AddRecurring<T>(name, every, factory)` enqueues a fresh job per interval, tracked in a RecurringJobState table so a restart never double-runs it (single catch-up if overdue); read the schedule back from `JobOptions.RecurringJobs` (public `RecurringJobDefinition` Name/Interval/Factory) and join it to RecurringJobState for last-fired, or call Factory() to enqueue an off-schedule run. Each job's outcome is saved on its OWN SaveChanges (not once per batch), so a row edited/deleted underneath the drain costs that one row instead of re-running everything the batch already executed; a failing poll is logged and retried rather than faulting the BackgroundService (which would stop the host). A source generator registers each IBackgroundJob type (name→Type) at module load for reflection-free rehydration. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskJobs<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval; MaxAttempts; AddRecurring(...); })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskJobs()` in OnModelCreating (maps Job + RecurringJobState) + `rask db add AddJobs && rask db update`. Server-side. MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands). the tutorial writes the IBackgroundJob record + handler.
- [Transactional email](docs/mail.md): the opt-in `Rask.Mail` package — durable transactional email queued on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Compose with a fluent `Email` builder (`Email.To(addr,name?).AndTo/.Cc/.Bcc/.ReplyTo/.From/.Subject/.Body(Component|string html)/.PlainText/.Attach`); `.Body(Component)` renders a Rask component to HTML IMMEDIATELY (Component.ToHtml()) so the persisted row is self-contained (no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency — nothing is rehydrated at send time). Addresses are validated at the call site (MimeKit MailboxAddress.TryParse) so a malformed address throws on build, not after MaxAttempts. Inject `IMail` and `SendAsync(email)` (asap) / `ScheduleAsync(email, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `QueuedMail` row (envelope + already-rendered HTML) via IDbContextFactory, defaulting From from MailOptions. The hosted `MailProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due messages (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), delivers each via the registered `IMailSender` resolved per message from a fresh scope (so a custom scoped sender isn't captured), stamps ProcessedAt PER MESSAGE (a save failure re-sends at most that one, never the batch); on failure Attempts++/Error + exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 10) → dead letter; a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per cycle so it never faults the host; sent rows purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d) via ExecuteDeleteAsync. `IMailSender` selection in AddRaskMail: `MailOptions.Smtp` set → `MailKitMailSender` (SMTP via MailKit); else `PickupDirectory` set → `PickupDirectoryMailSender` (writes .eml files); else `LogMailSender` — so it works ZERO-CONFIG in dev with no SMTP. Register your own IMailSender before AddRaskMail (any lifetime) to send via a provider API. Wire: `services.AddRaskMail<AppDbContext>(o => { o.From="..."; o.Smtp=new SmtpOptions{Host,Port,User,Password,Security}; o.PollInterval; o.MaxAttempts; })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` in OnModelCreating (maps QueuedMail) + `rask db add AddMail && rask db update`. References Rask.Core (Component.ToHtml) with PrivateAssets=all + MailKit; server-side; self-contained (no Rask.Jobs dependency). MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands).  an email body is a Rask component; register `AddRaskMail<Ctx>` in Program.cs and adds `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` to that context's OnModelCreating (idempotent), leaving only SMTP config + `rask db add/update`; with no context (or several, no flag) it prints the manual steps instead.
- [Cache](docs/cache.md): REDIS: `ICache` works over ANY IDistributedCache — `services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(...)` then the NON-GENERIC `services.AddRaskCache()` (no <TContext>), which registers ONLY ICache: no purger, no CacheEntry table, no migration. It takes NO CacheOptions on purpose — PurgeInterval and DefaultSlidingExpiration are implemented by the EF store, so against Redis they would silently do nothing; expiry is the store's business. There is deliberately NO Rask.Cache.Redis package (Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis is the standard API). Only the cache moves — jobs, mail and the outbox stay on the database because they need transactions.  the opt-in `Rask.Cache` package — a developer-facing cache on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Implements the standard `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Distributed.IDistributedCache` (Get/Set/Refresh/Remove + sync/async, `DistributedCacheEntryOptions` absolute/AbsoluteRelativeToNow/sliding) via `RaskDistributedCache<TContext>` — stores one `CacheEntry` row per key (Key PK, Value byte[], AbsoluteExpiration?, SlidingSeconds?, effective ExpiresAt, CreatedAt) through IDbContextFactory; a read past ExpiresAt is a MISS + lazily evicted, a read of a sliding entry RENEWS ExpiresAt (capped by any absolute deadline). Plus a typed `ICache`/`Cache` layer over it: `GetOrAddAsync<T>(key, factory, options?)` (factory runs once on a miss — not a lock, keep it idempotent), `GetAsync<T>`, `SetAsync<T>`, `RemoveAsync`, serializing T with System.Text.Json; the reflection overloads are `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`/`[RequiresDynamicCode]` and have trim-safe `JsonTypeInfo<T>` siblings (the byte[] IDistributedCache surface is fully trim-safe). The hosted `CachePurger<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer) bulk-deletes rows past ExpiresAt on PurgeInterval (default 5min) via ExecuteDeleteAsync — a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per sweep so it never faults the host. Wire: `services.AddRaskCache<AppDbContext>(o => { o.PurgeInterval; o.DefaultSlidingExpiration; })` (registers IDistributedCache + ICache + the purger, idempotent) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskCache()` in OnModelCreating (maps CacheEntry) + `rask db add AddCache && rask db update`. Server-side; one purger per app; no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency. Drops into ASP.NET session state (`AddSession()`) and anything else built on IDistributedCache. No per-instance artifact to scaffold.

- [Logging](docs/logging.md): the opt-in `Rask.Logging` package — a DURABLE log store in a SQLite file of its OWN (not the app's DbContext, no EF Core, no migration). `builder.Services.AddRaskLogging(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Logs") ?? "Data Source=logs.db", o => {...})` — scaffolded by `rask new` — the log store is on by default, `--no-logs` leaves it out; it takes a CONNECTION STRING rather than a `TContext`, which is the whole design: log lines arrive at machine rates and would put a high-frequency writer on the app database's single SQLite write lock, and the most valuable line is the one written WHILE A TRANSACTION IS FAILING — on the app's context that line rolls back with the failure. Trade-off, stated in the docs: `logs.db` is NOT covered by `rask db backup` or Litestream, and log lines can contain secrets. Registers a `[ProviderAlias("Rask")] ILoggerProvider` (via TryAddEnumerable, so a repeated call can't double-capture), so it sees exactly what every other sink sees — including the framework's `Rask.Live`/`Rask.Diff`/`Rask.Lifecycle` categories. PATH: a log call formats and `TryWrite`s into a bounded `Channel` (`BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite`, `QueueCapacity` 10_000) — it NEVER blocks or throws on the caller's thread; a full buffer DROPS the entry and counts it. The hosted `LogWriter` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer on `FlushInterval` 1s) drains it and inserts up to `BatchSize` (500) rows in ONE `InImmediateTransactionAsync` (Rask.SQLite's non-blocking, thread-yielding busy-retry) with a single re-bound prepared command; `StopAsync` drains what's buffered under `ShutdownDrainTimeout` (5s) before completing the channel, because the lines just before a shutdown are the ones worth keeping. RETENTION every `PurgeInterval` (1h): entries older than `Retention` (14d, `TimeSpan.Zero` = forever) then a trim to the newest `MaxRows` (100_000, 0 = uncapped) — BOTH by default, since age alone can't bound the disk under a storm; deleted in pages of 1000 looping until drained, so the write lock is never held for a whole sweep. SCHEMA is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS RaskLog` (Id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — a rowid alias, deliberately NOT AUTOINCREMENT; Timestamp TEXT round-trip "O" UTC so range filters are string compares and the file reads in a sqlite3 shell; Level INTEGER; Category; EventId; Message; Exception) + 3 indexes, created once behind a SemaphoreSlim, with the production pragmas (WAL matters: it's what lets the dashboard read while the writer flushes) applied on EVERY open. RE-ENTRANCY: `Rask.Logging*` and `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite*` are ALWAYS excluded from capture whatever `o.ExcludedCategories` says — otherwise a SQLite failure logs a line that fails to write that logs a line. `o.MinimumLevel` is a FLOOR, not an override (the pipeline applies `Logging:LogLevel` first). READ IT with `ILogs`: `QueryAsync(LogQuery{MinimumLevel, Category, Search, From, To, Page, PageSize})` → `LogPage(Entries newest-first, TotalCount, Page, PageSize, PageCount)`, plus `CategoriesAsync`/`CountAsync`/`PurgeAsync`/`ClearAsync`; LIKE wildcards in user text are escaped, so searching `100%` means a literal percent. METRICS on meter `Rask.Logging`: `rask.logs.written`, `rask.logs.dropped` (THE ONE TO ALERT ON — a full buffer OR a batch whose write failed; it is the only signal that the stored log is incomplete), `rask.logs.purged`, `rask.logs.stored` (sampled by the writer, not per observation). `rask deploy` sets `ConnectionStrings__Logs=Data Source=/data/logs.db` on the same volume as app.db. In `Rask.Dashboard`, `/_rask/logs` gains a **History** mode (paged, level/category/text filters) beside the always-present in-memory **Live** tail — two modes rather than a merged view because the writer flushes on an interval, so the newest lines are buffered but not yet on disk. Scopes are not captured (`BeginScope` returns null). Trim/AOT safe: no reflection, no serializer.
- [Cache](docs/cache.md): the opt-in `Rask.Cache` package — a developer-facing cache on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Implements the standard `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Distributed.IDistributedCache` (Get/Set/Refresh/Remove + sync/async, `DistributedCacheEntryOptions` absolute/AbsoluteRelativeToNow/sliding) via `RaskDistributedCache<TContext>` — stores one `CacheEntry` row per key (Key PK, Value byte[], AbsoluteExpiration?, SlidingSeconds?, effective ExpiresAt, CreatedAt) through IDbContextFactory; a read past ExpiresAt is a MISS + lazily evicted, a read of a sliding entry RENEWS ExpiresAt (capped by any absolute deadline). The hosted `CachePurger<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer) bulk-deletes rows past ExpiresAt on PurgeInterval (default 5min) via ExecuteDeleteAsync — a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per sweep so it never faults the host. Wire: `services.AddRaskCache<AppDbContext>(o => { o.PurgeInterval; o.DefaultSlidingExpiration; })` (registers IDistributedCache + ICache + the purger, idempotent) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskCache()` in OnModelCreating (maps CacheEntry) + `rask db add AddCache && rask db update`. Server-side; one purger per app; no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency. Drops into ASP.NET session state (`AddSession()`) and anything else built on IDistributedCache. No per-instance artifact to scaffold.
- [Mobile & PWA](docs/pwa.md): build installable mobile apps in C#. WASM = full PWA (install, true offline, push, every device API). Server = installable + push-capable via AddRaskPwa (serves manifest + service worker, auto-registers it, emits the manifest link into the server-rendered head), but NOT an offline app (offline navigations show a static offline.html; no background sync; install-prompt + activation-bound device APIs stay WASM-only). Typed Web app manifest (WebAppManifest in Rask.Core.Browser; WASM UsePwa / Server AddRaskPwa), default service worker (rask-sw.js; shared push/notificationclick handlers in Rask.Core), IWebPush + INotifications + IBadge + IWakeLock (Rask.Core.Browser, both hosts), `rask new MyApp --template wasm --pwa` / `rask new MyApp --pwa`. Sending push from the backend: the opt-in `Rask.WebPush` package (IWebPush, VAPID RFC 8292 + aes128gcm RFC 8291, zero external deps) — full reference in [Web Push](docs/webpush.md).
- [Web Push (server send)](docs/webpush.md): the opt-in Rask.WebPush package delivers a Web Push notification from your backend, zero external deps. VapidKeys.Generate() mints a base64url P-256 pair (RFC 8292; PublicKey IS the browser's applicationServerKey, hand the same string to the client IWebPush.SubscribeAsync); AddRaskWebPush(o => { o.VapidKeys; o.Subject = mailto:/https: }) validates at startup; store the client's PushSubscription(Endpoint, P256dh, Auth); IWebPush.SendAsync(sub, WebPushMessage.Text(title, body, url)) returns a WebPushResult (IsSuccess; ShouldDelete on 404/410 — prune it; ShouldRetry on 429/5xx). Typed WebPushMessage fields serialize to the default rask-sw.js JSON {title,body,icon,badge,tag,data.url}; RawPayload is the escape hatch; Urgency/Ttl/Topic map to RFC 8030 semantics; payloads encrypted with aes128gcm (RFC 8291). Standalone server library — no Rask.Core/Rask.Wasm dependency.
- [Observability](docs/observability.md): structured logging, the `Rask.Server` meter + activity source, `AddRaskLiveSessions()` health check.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): `RaskLiveOptions` (shared: diff mode, path base, session cap) + `RaskServerOptions` (server-only WS/grace/idle/backpressure limits) + `RaskUploadOptions` (upload size + per-session quota), appsettings binding + startup validation.
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): containerizing the apps — opt-in `--docker` on the three web templates scaffolds a production multi-stage Dockerfile (+ `.dockerignore`): the `server` template builds on the .NET SDK image and run on `aspnet:10.0` (non-root, port 8080, `UseHttpsRedirection` no-ops in-container so terminate TLS at the proxy and forward the WebSocket upgrade); the standalone `wasm` bundle publishes then serves from `nginx:alpine` with a bundled `nginx.conf` (SPA `try_files` fallback, `application/wasm` MIME, `gzip_static` for the baked `*.gz`). GitHub Pages / sub-path via `/p:RaskPathBase=`. One-command deploy of that Dockerfile: `rask deploy --host root@box [--domain app.example.com]` builds the image on the box over SSH and runs it — with `--domain` a shared Caddy proxy adds automatic HTTPS and deploys are zero-downtime (blue-green), multiple apps to one host. Point it at a **bare VPS** (root + SSH key, nothing else) and it prepares the box first — Docker, a non-root `deploy` login, ufw, SSH hardening — after showing the plan and asking once, so you never SSH in yourself; `rask deploy --github-actions` writes the workflow that repeats it on every push. Note ufw does **not** filter Docker-published ports (docker writes its own iptables rules): that's benign here because the only published ports are the intended-public ones (Caddy's 80/443, or `--port`), but an unrelated `-p` container won't be hidden by `ufw deny`.
- [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): ARIA via the `Aria` dictionary, `Role`/`TabIndex`, `Lang`/`Dir` for WCAG 3.1.2 (Language of Parts) and `Hidden`/`Inert`, the `Img` alt-text analyzer (RASK023), and automatic navigation a11y on the Server host (SPA route changes show a progress bar, move focus into the new page's `<main>`, and announce the route via `aria-live`).
- [Localization](docs/localization.md): ship in more than one language. Configured ONLY in Program.cs — `AddRask(configureCulture: c => c.SupportedCultures.Add("hu"))`, the FIRST entry being the default. There is NO --culture flag and no --no-localization (#854): a scaffolded server app already registers "en" there and adding a language is a line in that block, so a flag would only restate at scaffold time what the file goes on being the truth about. A visitor's language is negotiated `?culture=` → cookie → `Accept-Language`/`navigator.languages` → default, settled BEFORE the first render on both hosts (the server's first HTML byte already carries `lang="hu"`), and then owned by their session rather than the thread — which is why it survives the framework's deliberate `ExecutionContext.SuppressFlow()`. **URLs stay culture-neutral**: one link is the same page for everyone, and the router/`Url()`/`Go()` are untouched. The cookie is ASP.NET's own `.AspNetCore.Culture` in ASP.NET's own format, so an app also calling `UseRequestLocalization()` agrees with it. Text lives in `Resources/Strings.{culture}.json` and compiles to typed members: `Strings.Greeting(name)`, where a typo'd key is CS0117 and a wrong argument count CS1501 — no reflection, no satellite assemblies, so it works under `InvariantGlobalization` too (only date/number formatting falls back). Placeholders are named (`{name}`, `{count:int}`, `{price:decimal:C}`) because other languages reorder arguments; a mismatched placeholder SET is RASK051 (error, it would throw `FormatException` in that one language), a missing translation is RASK052 (warning, neutral text is used — promote it in `.editorconfig` to gate a release). Counts use `{ "$plural": "count", "one": …, "other": … }` with a curated CLDR table; the required fallback is the language's own residual, which is `many` for Polish and Russian rather than `other`, and a language Rask does not carry is a build error naming it. Components read `Culture`/`UICulture`/`IsRightToLeft`, which also marks them so a switch repaints. Wire formats stay invariant on purpose (`<input type=date|number>`, route values, reconciliation keys — the browser localizes typed inputs itself). `<html lang>` follows the session and `dir="rtl"` is emitted only for RTL; an app that names no language renders byte-identical HTML to before. WASM needs `<RaskGlobalization>true</RaskGlobalization>` for ICU (~2.6 MB of `icudt*.dat`; +3.92 MB raw / +1.05 MB brotli on a published bundle once the larger non-invariant runtime is counted), which also clears `PredefinedCulturesOnly` — otherwise `GetCultureInfo("hu-HU")` throws rather than falling back. a browser-WASM app scaffolds NO culture registration and carries `<RaskGlobalization>` COMMENTED OUT with the reason beside it, so shipping a language there is two deliberate edits — uncomment the property, add the languages in Program.cs: catalogs without ICU are a no-op, because the resolver refuses to let a culture pose as supported when the data isn't there, so the app would boot with an EMPTY supported list and warn once at startup (#846 — both WASM generators used to accept `--culture` and emit nothing at all). The framework's own text (picker chrome, 404, error page) translates via a reserved `Resources/RaskStrings.{culture}.json` whose keys are `RaskString` members, registered by a generated module initializer with no wiring.
- [Migration from Blazor](docs/migration-from-blazor.md): mapping Blazor concepts to Rask.
- [Diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md): RASK001–043 compile-time diagnostics + fixes, including IDE quick-fixes (lightbulb) for RASK001 (add `required`), RASK023 (insert `Alt: ""`) and CS0108 (add `new` to a member hiding a builder entry), shipped in `Rask.Generators.CodeFixes`.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): the `Rask.Testing` package (`RaskTest.Render(component)` → `RenderedComponent`, adding no markup of its own, and `RaskTest.RenderDocument(app, services?)` when the assertion is about the PAGE — it renders a root the way a host does, document composed around it, so `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang>`, the collected `<head>` and `<body class>` are all assertable; `.ClickAsync()`/`.InvokeAsync(handlerId, json?)` dispatch handlers + re-render; `.Html`/`.HandlerId`/`.Attr` query) for in-process component unit tests, plus Playwright E2E patterns. Render MOUNTS the component (OnMount, OnMountAsync, OnRendered, OnUnmount all fire) and gives it a render handle, so state set after an await in an async lifecycle hook reaches the markup; for a component that loads in OnMountAsync use `await page.WaitForAsync("text" | predicate, timeout?)` — it re-renders until the markup matches and throws a TimeoutException carrying the last markup, rather than a fixed delay. Note `Text` HTML-encodes non-ASCII, so an ellipsis in a placeholder ("Reading…") is NOT a literal substring of `.Html`.

## Contributing to Rask itself
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repo conventions for AI assistants + the `.claude/skills/` workflows.
- [Development workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): the format → warnings-as-errors → tests →
  benchmarks → docs → review → PR gate, CI, nightly, analyzers.
- [Code analysis](docs/code-analysis.md): analyzers and adoption.
- [Public API style](docs/api-style.md): the naming rules every public member obeys, and the PublicAPI.txt gate that enforces them.
